Run a grid of simulation scenarios

Source: R/workflow.R
run_scenarios.Rd

Runs every row of scenarios in every replicate and returns one table. Each replicate draws what setup returns once, so scenarios are compared on the same tree and landscape. Each cell of the design has its own seed, which comes from seed, its replicate and its row, so results do not depend on the order of the cells nor on the number of workers. Cells run in parallel under a plan of the future package, if you choose one. The random number generator of the session is left as it was.

Usage

run_scenarios(
  scenarios,
  simulate,
  setup = NULL,
  summarise = function(sim, shared) summary_stats(sim, shared$tree),
  n_rep = 1,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

scenarios

Data frame with one scenario per row and one parameter per column.

simulate

Function of scenario, a list with one row of scenarios, and shared, what setup returned, which gives a simulation.

setup

Optional function without arguments that draws what the scenarios of one replicate share, such as a list with tree and landscape.

summarise

Function of sim and shared that gives a named numeric vector. The default is summary_stats(), with shared$tree if there is one.

n_rep

Number of replicates.

seed

Integer that sets all the seeds.

Value

Data frame with the columns of scenarios, replicate and the statistics.

See also

Other simulation studies: as.data.frame.mc_sim(), equilibrium_check(), summary_stats()

Examples

scenarios <- expand.grid(dispersal = c(0.001, 0.1), lambda = c(0, 1))
shared_pool <- function() {
  list(tree = treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(10), landscape = landscape_implicit(8))
}
one_run <- function(scenario, shared) {
  simulate_metacommunity(shared$landscape, species_traits(shared$tree, scenario$lambda),
                         competition_matrix(shared$tree, "none"),
                         dispersal = scenario$dispersal, n_steps = 30, seed_steps = 1:3)
}
out <- run_scenarios(scenarios, one_run, shared_pool, n_rep = 2)
aggregate(alpha ~ dispersal + lambda, out, mean)
#>   dispersal lambda  alpha
#> 1     0.001      0 2.6250
#> 2     0.100      0 5.5625
#> 3     0.001      1 3.6875
#> 4     0.100      1 5.8125
